taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Andropogon gerardi Vitman. The widespread North American spelling Andropogon gerardii is retained as a primary alias/search term because it remains standard in many Texas and U.S. references.
look_here_first: Start at the top: big bluestem usually has 2–6 fingerlike racemes radiating together, often forming the classic turkey-foot. It is a tall robust prairie grass, not a fluffy plume.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County Ranch native tallgrass documentation; Texas Conservation Action Plan Travis County Blackland Prairie community documentation; NPSOT Williamson County locally sourced historic prairie seed provenance.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: All three counties are explicitly named by project-acceptable sources; no broad prairie-range inference.

best_field_traits: 2–6 digitate racemes at the culm tip
classic turkey-foot silhouette when 3 principal racemes are developed
leaf blades roughly 5–10 mm wide in GrassBase
racemes exposed rather than densely enclosed in upper sheaths
open-fingered inflorescence rather than woolly or broomlike
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Bushy bluestem forms dense fluffy clusters near the top; broomsedge has narrow silky racemes partly enclosed by spathe-like sheaths. Big bluestem instead has a few exposed digitate racemes forming a turkey-foot.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Bushy bluestem forms dense fluffy clusters near the top; broomsedge has narrow silky racemes partly enclosed by spathe-like sheaths. Big bluestem instead has a few exposed digitate racemes forming a turkey-foot.
